stem:
Hector has four circles that are the same size. He divided and shaded the first circle to represent the fraction \(\frac{4}{6}\).

Hector will correctly divide and shade the other circles to represent fractions less than \(\frac{4}{6}\).

Which answer choice is NOT a way Hector could divide and shade a circle to represent a fraction less than \(\frac{4}{6}\)?

options.label: A
options.text: He could divide a circle into 6 equal parts and shade 1 of the parts.

options.label: B
options.text: He could divide a circle into 8 equal parts and shade 4 of the parts.

options.label: C
options.text: He could divide a circle into 4 equal parts and shade 4 of the parts.

options.label: D
options.text: He could divide a circle into 6 equal parts and shade 3 of the parts.

visual_elements: Four circles with only the first circle divided into 6 equal parts with 4 parts shaded.
difficulty_rationale: The problem requires understanding fractions and comparing fractions with different denominators, which involves more than straightforward recall but not multi-step reasoning.
